claim_under_attack.mission_md_claim: Hydrophobic-vs-hydrophilic classification works: 71% accuracy on held-out test is a useful screening signal even when regression MAE is modest -- the coating IP decision 'hydrophobic candidate: yes/no' is often what actually matters for anti-biofouling screening.
claim_under_attack.mission_md_location: SCIENTIFIC INTERPRETATION, point 3 (section 'Empirical benchmark result -- OpenPoly water contact angle ML baseline')

fire_sequence: ROTATION fire. Read the module's full falsification-ledger history (46 prior amphora-molecule-property entries, 2026-08-01 through 2026-08-17) and cross-referenced against evidence/phase0/kpis/ (21 KPI files) and RETRACTION-INDEX.md. Identified openpoly-water-contact-angle-ml-baseline-kpi.v1.json as never before ledger-attacked (unlike its sibling openpoly-dielectric-constant-ml-baseline-kpi.v1.json, which has been macro-bisected, admissibility-audited, and physically-audited three times). Read the KPI and its docs/mission.md narrative in full: 9 of its 10 deterministic gates are honestly self-critical (LOSO-CV positive, holdout MAE explicitly documented as WORSE than NULL), but gate 10 (hydrophobic_classification_accuracy_at_least_0_7, floor=0.7, PASSED at 0.711) and mission.md's SCIENTIFIC INTERPRETATION point 3 ('Hydrophobic-vs-hydrophilic classification works... a useful screening signal') assert a working classifier with no comparison to a trivial baseline -- unlike this KPI's OWN MAE metrics, which all carry an explicit NULL-median baseline. That asymmetry is the attack surface: an imbalanced binary target (27/38 test molecules are NOT hydrophobic) can pass a bare accuracy floor by base rate alone.
method: Independently reconstructed the tp/fp/fn/tn confusion matrix from the scientific receipt's own 38 per-molecule held_out_test_records (actual_hydrophobic vs predicted_hydrophobic booleans, theta>90deg threshold per Cassie 1948/Baier 1970), NOT from the pre-aggregated summary numbers in the KPI file, then computed: (1) the trivial majority-class-only baseline accuracy on the SAME 38 records; (2) balanced accuracy (average of per-class recall, corrects for class imbalance); (3) Matthews correlation coefficient (Matthews 1975, chance-corrected agreement for binary classification); (4) a two-sided Fisher exact test (Fisher 1922) on the 2x2 prediction-vs-actual table, testing the null hypothesis that predicted class is statistically independent of actual class.
objective: Test whether the KPI's hydrophobic_classification_accuracy_at_least_0_7 gate (PASSED, 0.711 >= 0.7) and the mission.md claim that this classification 'works' and is 'a useful screening signal' reflect genuine structure-to-property signal, or are fully explained by class-imbalance base rate (predicting the majority class for every molecule).
pre_registered_refute_criterion: The classification gate/claim is REFUTED as evidence of a working classifier if the model's holdout accuracy is bitwise-identical to the trivial majority-class-only baseline accuracy on the SAME test set, AND a two-sided Fisher exact test on the prediction-vs-actual 2x2 table fails to reject independence at alpha=0.05 (i.e. the predictions are not statistically distinguishable from being drawn independently of the true label).
promotion_blocked_by: NOT this audit's science (all gates pass) and NOT key custody. Manifest untouched.
recommended_followups: Repair the gate definition: replace the bare hydrophobic_classification_accuracy_at_least_0_7 floor with a chance-corrected metric (balanced accuracy or MCC) plus an explicit majority-baseline comparison, mirroring the null-median pattern already used for the MAE gates in this same KPI.

Correct docs/mission.md SCIENTIFIC INTERPRETATION point 3 to stop asserting the classifier 'works' as a screening signal; either retract the framing or re-run with a recall-sensitive threshold (e.g. cost-weighted or precision-recall-optimized cutoff) and report against the majority baseline honestly.

The same base-rate-vs-floor gate pattern may exist on other binary/threshold gates elsewhere in this module's 21 KPI files -- worth a follow-up sweep for any other floor-only accuracy gate lacking a baseline comparison.

rights_check: No new data source opened. This audit reads only the already-in-tree scientific receipt and KPI files already consumed and pinned by sha256 in the module. No quarantined or CONTEXT_ONLY source was opened.
scope_note: This does NOT refute the KPI's LOSO-CV regression result (best_LOSO_result R2=+0.0781, MAE beats NULL by 6.0% across 66 folds) or the honestly-disclosed holdout regression underperformance (both left untouched, both already correctly characterized in mission.md as a 'MIXED FINDING'). self_check_pure_majority_guess.purpose: Confirms the real observed result is checker-indistinguishable from an explicit 'always predict not-hydrophobic' rule applied to the SAME 38 test molecules, not merely numerically close to it.

self_check_synthetic_informative_classif.expected: accuracy clearly exceeds majority baseline; Fisher p < 0.05; balanced accuracy clearly > 0.5
self_check_synthetic_informative_classif.purpose: Confirms the SAME checker (majority-baseline-equivalence + Fisher exact test) has real discriminating power and is not vacuously firing REFUTED on any input. Synthetic confusion matrix tp=8,fp=3,fn=3,tn=24 (n=38, same 11/27 base rate as the real data) simulates a classifier that genuinely tracks the label.

why: Independently reconstructing the confusion matrix from the scientific receipt's own 38 held_out_test_records reproduces the published tp=1/fp=1/fn=10/tn=26 and accuracy=0.7105263157894737 exactly (rederived_accuracy_matches_kpi_published_accuracy=true), confirming the published numbers are real, not fabricated. But the model's accuracy (0.7105263158) is bitwise-identical to the trivial always-predict-not-hydrophobic majority baseline (0.7105263158) on the identical 38-molecule test set: model_accuracy_equals_majority_baseline_bitwise=true, self_check_pure_majority_guess confirms this is not coincidental proximity but exact numerical equivalence to a rule that ignores molecular structure entirely. Balanced accuracy is 0.5269 (chance=0.5000, only +0.0269 above chance); Matthews correlation coefficient is 0.1094 (weak); the two-sided Fisher exact test on the prediction-vs-actual table gives p=0.5007, far from significant at alpha=0.05 -- the null hypothesis that predictions are independent of true class CANNOT be rejected. recall on the positive (hydrophobic) class is 0.091 (1 of 11 true hydrophobic polymers correctly flagged); precision=0.5 is driven by a single true positive against a single false positive. The self-check against a synthetic genuinely-informative classifier (same n=38, same 11/27 base rate, tp=8/fp=3/fn=3/tn=24) confirms the SAME checker correctly detects real skill when present (accuracy 0.842 clearly exceeds the 0.711 majority baseline, Fisher p=0.0004, balanced accuracy 0.808) -- so this is not a vacuous attack that would fire REFUTED on any input. The mission.md claim ('classification works... a useful screening signal... often what actually matters') and the KPI gate's PASSED status both overstate what the held-out evidence supports: on the single evaluation this KPI actually reports (the 38-molecule scaffold-safe holdout), the classifier's decisions carry no statistically demonstrable information about true hydrophobicity beyond the base rate.
